builder_plan.scenario: Your workload might fit a smaller or differently structured model.
builder_plan.change: Check for available weights and a compatible runtime before planning a product trial.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current model on identical held-out tasks and the same resource budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, latency, memory, context limits, and migration cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: SPARTA: A Sparse Ternary LLM Accelerator with Adaptive Attention and Unified Datapath for Long-Context Edge Inference
summary: SPARTA replaces conventional GPU/CPU edge inference and separate ternary-linear and attention datapaths with a custom unified accelerator combining ternary-weight SpMM/SpMV, bit-serial attention, and page-level Top-k plus token-level Top-p KV-cache pruning. Its gains depend on fabricating or programming dedicated hardware and on 1.58-bit ternary models, and the adaptive attention prunes KV access at the cost of task-dependent quality loss. It can fail in applicability terms: the results are accelerator-specific, quality degradation varies by task and pruning aggressiveness, and nothing here transfers directly to a 24 GB GPU or API-based stack.
rationale: The technique is a custom hardware accelerator, not deployable software, so a practitioner limited to one GPU or third-party APIs cannot adopt it, though its sparse-attention and ternary trends are worth tracking as they reach commodity software stacks.
technique: Sparse ternary accelerator with adaptive sparse attention

claims.statement: SPARTA replaces conventional GPU/CPU edge inference and separate ternary-linear and attention datapaths with a custom unified accelerator combining ternary-weight SpMM/SpMV, bit-serial attention, and page-level Top-k plus token-level Top-p KV-cache pruning. Its gains depend on fabricating or programming dedicated hardware and on 1.58-bit ternary models, and the adaptive attention prunes KV access at the cost of task-dependent quality loss. It can fail in applicability terms: the results are accelerator-specific, quality degradation varies by task and pruning aggressiveness, and nothing here transfers directly to a 24 GB GPU or API-based stack.
3.9x higher generation throughput and 8.3x higher end-to-end energy efficiency versus NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin; 4.1-4.8x KV-traffic reduction over full attention, with task-dependent quality loss.
